data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2020 were GBP 1,123.995m. Using the syndicate's gross claims development table (cumulative gross claims incurred), estimated prior-year development (years 2018 and older) shows a net adverse reestimate of approximately GBP 24.6m (around 2.19% of opening reserves), i.e. a strengthening of reserves. The syndicate reports significant 2020 impacts from the COVID-19 pandemic (additional gross losses of GBP 201.7m, net GBP 152.7m) and GBP 18.4m of 2020 natural catastrophe losses (Derecho storms and Hurricane Laura). Historic prior-year movements referenced in the report include natural catastrophe-driven net losses in 2016, 2017 and 2018 and higher than expected prioryears' development affecting 2019. The prior-year development figure above is calculated from the published gross claims development triangle and excludes the two most recent underwriting years per the standard methodology.
raw_causal_phrases: unprecedented loss in relation to the COVID-19 global pandemic of GBP 152.7m
GBP 18.4m loss in relation to 2020 natural catastrophes (Derecho storms and hurricane Laura)
higher than expected losses on prior years of account
The decrease in reinsurers' share of claims outstanding during 2020 was primarily due to the settlement of claims and proactive collection of reinsurance recoveries.
The 2016 year was impacted by natural catastrophe losses on the Alberta wildfires and hurricane Matthew with net losses of GBP 17.9m.

The 2017 year was impacted by several natural catastrophes with net losses of GBP 74.6m; hurricane Harvey; hurricane Irma; hurricane Maria; Mexico earthquake; Northern and Southern California wildfires.
The 2018 year was impacted by natural catastrophe net losses of GBP 22.8m; California Wildfires; hurricane Florence; hurricane Michael.

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (liabilities) 2019 comparative column. Prior-year development was calculated from the published GROSS claims development triangle (pages 39) by comparing each UW year's current estimate to the previous diagonal and summing for UW years 2011-2018 (excluding 'All prior years' aggregate and the two most recent underwriting years 2019-2020). The report does not present a standalone labelled 'movement in prior year's provision' gross figure; the triangle was used (confidence 0.8). Some event amounts quoted in the report are presented net of reinsurance; where the report explicitly states gross vs net this is noted. The syndicate executed a transfer/reinsurance arrangement with Lloyd's Brussels on 30 Dec 2020 (RITC-style transfer and 100% quota share reinsurance) - the combined economic effect was reported as nil but this corporate activity could affect presentation; no material distortion of the triangle was identified. Lob-level reserve movements are not quantified in the report; lob movements above are inferred with low-to-moderate confidence.
